claims.text: DFT-based two-phase coexistence or interface-pinning simulations can accurately calculate melting temperatures for high-melting refractory materials.
The proposed method can calculate entropy of fusion.
The proposed method can calculate enthalpy of fusion.
The proposed method can calculate volume change at the melting point.
The proposed method significantly reduces computational cost relative to full ab initio thermodynamic integration.
The simulation protocol directly samples a solid–liquid interface.
Solid and liquid phases coexist in equilibrium under simulation conditions close to the melting point.
The solid–liquid interfacial region mediates the phase transformation.
Equilibrating coexisting solid and liquid phases directly retrieves their free-energy differences.
The melting properties can be extracted without computationally expensive thermodynamic integration.
The calculated melting properties will agree with full ab initio thermodynamic-integration results within simulation uncertainty.
The reduction in computational cost will make the method more feasible for high-throughput applications.
The method works effectively when a clear, stable solid–liquid interface can be maintained.
Complex phase behavior or inadequately captured interface effects may limit the method.
Computational savings and prediction errors may vary with the material and simulation setup.
